description: Negative, DEPRECATED SPELLING: clinical:CoverageRecord with no clinical:providerName, so the coverage identifies no insurer

input.payorName: Blue Cross Blue Shield of Oregon

shaclConstraintViolated: clinical:CoverageRecordShape / path clinical:providerName / MinCountConstraintComponent, sh:minCount 1 at sh:Violation :: "Insurance provider name is required on a coverage record"
notes: The negative half of legacycoverage-001, proving clinical:CoverageRecordShape FIRES rather than merely being present. Everything else about the record is well-formed, and apart from the subject IRI and health:sourceRecordId -- which must differ so the two fixtures are not mistaken for one record -- it is field-for-field identical to the happy path, clinical:payorName included. So the single reported violation is attributable to the one removed field. clinical:providerName is one of the shape's FIVE sh:Violation constraints, not three: clinical:memberId and clinical:coverageType carry sh:severity sh:Violation explicitly, while cascade:dataProvenance and cascade:schemaVersion declare no sh:severity at all and so take SHACL's default, which is sh:Violation. providerName is the one whose absence has a stated consequence: the shape's own message is that without it the record identifies no coverage and cannot be reconciled against a claim. Note the property is cross-class since clinical v1.16, which dropped its rdfs:domain because encounters and documents carry it too; that is exactly why the coverage-specific requirement is stated in SHACL here rather than in the ontology, and clinical.ttl's comment says so. Measured RED against a spec revision before clinical v1.18: no shape targeted clinical:CoverageRecord at all, so this record validated conforms:true and the runner reported the fixture UNSHAPED rather than accepting it.
